name: stark-accessibility
description: Five role-specific accessibility agents (front-end, back-end, mobile, design, PM) backed by the Stark Continuous Accessibility platform.

positive.description: Find the project that needs the most accessibility work
positive.prompt: In our Stark Grow Demos team, which project has the most open accessibility violations, and what's the main issue category there?
positive.expected_behavior: Identifies Figma "Hide frames" test as the project with the most open violations (over 2,000) and Reflow & Zoom as its top issue category, with [Design System] Include Elements (roughly 450) as the next highest. Links to the projects in Stark.

positive.description: Explain a URL asset's violations and give code fixes
positive.prompt: Show me the accessibility violations on the "www.getstark.co and 2 more" URL asset in our Team Sync project, and give me code fixes for the most serious ones.
positive.expected_behavior: Summarizes the violations across the asset's three scanned pages, including text below the 4.5:1 contrast minimum, an img with no alt or title attribute, content outside landmark elements, and a redundant aria-checked attribute. Gives before/after code fixes for the high-severity issues and cites the WCAG criteria Stark returns for each, such as 1.1.1 Non-text Content for the missing alt and 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) for the text contrast.

positive.description: Summarize compliance status without certifying compliance
positive.prompt: What's the compliance status for Stark Grow Demos, and what still needs attention?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the team's Compliance Center frameworks and their scores (Stark Universal Accessibility Framework, W3C Accessibility Maturity Model (Draft), and European Accessibility Act), lists the incomplete controls assigned to the signed-in user, including Accessibility Statement approved, and links to the Compliance Center. Does not state that the organization is or isn't compliant.

positive.prompt: In our Team Sync project in Stark Grow Demos, create a new URL asset that monitors https://www.getstark.co/pricing.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a new URL asset for https://www.getstark.co/pricing in the existing Team Sync project, without creating a new project, and confirms it with a link. Because a www.getstark.co asset already exists, Stark may add a number to the new asset's name. Notes that results appear once Stark's scan completes.

positive.description: Turn Figma contrast failures into design guidance
positive.prompt: Which text in our TeamSync Design System Library Figma file fails color contrast, and how should our designers fix it?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the text contrast failures in the TeamSync Design System Library Figma asset (10 at submission) under WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA, identified by Figma layer. Explains the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text and 3:1 for large text, and recommends fixing the shared color styles or tokens. Does not invent colors or contrast ratios that Stark didn't return.

negative.description: Declines to certify legal compliance. Stark reports accessibility data but can't make a legal determination. Expected: declines the yes/no answer, gives the current status from Stark, and recommends review by a qualified person.
negative.prompt: Is our website ADA compliant? Just give me a yes or no.

negative.description: Doesn't access another organization's data. Expected: explains it can only access Stark teams the signed-in account belongs to, and returns no data from any other organization.
negative.prompt: Show me Acme Corp's accessibility violations in Stark.

negative.description: Can't delete Stark data. No delete tool exists. Expected: explains that deleting projects isn't available through this connection, calls no write tool, and points the user to the Stark app.
negative.prompt: Delete the Team Sync project in Stark.

review.commerce_description: Stark doesn't sell products or process payments through this plugin.

publication.release_notes: Adds five role-specific accessibility skills (front-end, back-end, mobile, design, and program management) that work with the Stark MCP connection, plus updated listing metadata, branding, review test cases, and a demo walkthrough.

interface.longDescription: Connect your Stark workspace to scan Figma files, code, Storybook, mobile apps, automated tests, and live URLs, then pull violations with full context and get role-specific fixes for front-end, back-end, mobile, design, and program management. Every call is scoped to the signed-in user's Stark organization.
defaultPrompt: Use Stark to show which projects have the most open accessibility violations and what to fix first.
Use Stark to pull the violations on our marketing site URL asset and give me code-level fixes.
Use Stark to summarize our compliance status and which framework controls need attention.
